lantern-cart.pitch: Churros, kettle corn and frozen lemonade from a cart in the middle of the plaza.
description: The cart parks under the lantern strings near the carousel. It is the quickest snack in the park and the last one open at night.

abuelas-cocina.pitch: The village restaurant: enchiladas, carne asada and guacamole made at the table.
description: Abuela's Cocina is the sit-down meal most families plan their day around. The dining room is tiled and loud in a good way, and the guacamole cart comes to you. Reservations are recommended, especially at lunch.

cuentos-toy-workshop.pitch: A toy shop where the shelves are low and everything can be picked up.
description: The workshop sells plush, building sets and bubble blasters. Farol the lighthouse cat lives here, in several sizes.

churro-corner.pitch: A snack window on the village square, known for the obvious.
description: Churros come out hot all day. The window also does corn dogs, nachos and frozen lemonade for anyone who is not here for the churros.

firefly-grill.pitch: Burgers, tenders and salads under the trees, with most of the seating in the shade.
description: Firefly Grill is the counter-service stop in the forest. The patio lights up with the canopy after dark, which makes it a pleasant place for a late dinner.

glow-grove-gifts.pitch: Park shirts, hats and sweets, plus anything that glows.
description: The shop sits at the exit of the caverns. Light-up toys sell fastest just before sunset.

the-pearl-table.pitch: Seafood on the lagoon, with window tables that face the evening show.
description: The Pearl Table is the finest meal inside Costa Encandela: blackened redfish, crab cakes and lobster bisque. Book the last seating if you want to watch the Sirena Lagoon Spectacular from your table.

tidepool-treats.pitch: Cold drinks and quick snacks beside the splash garden.
description: Parents tend to end up here while the kids run through the fountains. Frozen lemonade is the bestseller for a reason.

sirenas-treasures.pitch: Shells, sweets and souvenirs at the edge of the bay.
description: Sirena's Treasures carries the park's shirts, hats and ponchos, and does a steady trade in dry T-shirts for people coming out of the splash garden.

smugglers-galley.pitch: Tacos, burrito bowls and Cuban sandwiches from the galley on the dock.
description: The galley is the fastest lunch in Puerto Viejo. Order at the counter and eat at the long tables on the dock, where the Mercado Players sometimes wander through.

mercado-trading-post.pitch: The port's general store, stacked to the rafters.
description: Shirts, hats, pins and sweets, sold from market stalls under one roof.

dockside-lemonade.pitch: A lemonade stand on the dock that also does churros and corn dogs.
description: Small, fast and usually the shortest line for a cold drink on this side of the park.

starfall-diner.pitch: An air-conditioned diner under a ceiling of stars.
description: Starfall Diner serves burgers, tenders, salads and mac and cheese. It is the coolest place to sit in Costa Encandela at two in the afternoon.

constellation-outfitters.pitch: The shop at the coaster exit, for shirts that prove you rode it.
description: Park apparel, pins and sweets. The Constellation Coaster pin is sold here and at The Pin Exchange on the Paseo.

cloud-cones.pitch: Cotton candy and frozen drinks from a stand shaped like a cloud.
description: A quick stop between rides. The cotton candy is spun to order.

pier-supply-co.pitch: The first and last shop in the park, right on the boardwalk.
description: Pier Supply Co. carries Isla Velaluz shirts, hats and hoodies, along with ponchos for the water rides.

boardwalk-fry-house.pitch: Burgers, tenders and fries at a boardwalk counter.
description: Classic pier food, eaten at picnic tables over the water. Watch the gulls.

squall-snacks.pitch: Corn dogs, nachos and cold drinks at the foot of the wheel.
description: A snack window for people waiting on riders. Kettle corn travels well.

the-rivet-room.pitch: Ribs, salmon and a tower of onion rings in the old machine shop.
description: The Rivet Room is the sit-down restaurant on the wharf, with booths, steel beams and a view of The Anvil through the windows. Reservations are recommended at dinner.

foundry-eats.pitch: Counter-service burgers and salads next to the dodgems.
description: Foundry Eats is quick, indoors and close to everything on the wharf.

ironworks-gear.pitch: Shirts, hats and hoodies for people who just got off The Anvil.
description: The wharf's shop stocks the full Isla Velaluz apparel line and a wall of pins.

whirlpool-tacos.pitch: Tacos, bowls and Cuban sandwiches steps from the water rides.
description: Order at the window and dry off on the patio. Rice and beans come with everything.

cove-coolers.pitch: Frozen lemonade and snacks at the exit of the rapids.
description: The stand does its best business with people who are soaked and happy about it.

nimbus-noodle-bar.pitch: Ramen, dan dan noodles and bao on the ridge.
description: Nimbus Noodle Bar is the most unusual counter in the park and one of the most popular. Bowls come out fast, and the terrace looks down over the coasters.

skybreak-outfitters.pitch: The ridge-top shop for shirts, hoodies and pins.
description: Skybreak Outfitters carries Isla Velaluz apparel and the pins for the rides up here.

updraft-pretzels.pitch: Snacks and cold drinks between the towers.
description: A stand for the gap between rides. The line is rarely more than a few people.

trueno-cantina.pitch: Carne asada, fish tacos and tableside guacamole inside the research station.
description: Trueno Cantina is the sit-down restaurant in Cabo Trueno. The windows look out at the storm wall, and the room rumbles now and then. Reservations fill early in the day.

cabo-street-kitchen.pitch: Tacos, burrito bowls and plantain chips from a counter in the outpost.
description: The quick option in Cabo Trueno, with covered seating that stays dry when the weather turns.

tormenta-traders.pitch: The outpost's supply store: shirts, hats, pins and ponchos.
description: Tormenta Traders sits at the exit of Trueno Rally and carries the Isla Velaluz line.

thunder-ice.pitch: Frozen lemonade and snacks at the edge of the storm.
description: A stand near the coaster entrance. Frozen drinks sell out on the hottest afternoons.

tortuga-beach-shack.pitch: Burgers, tenders and fries, served to people in swimsuits.
description: The Beach Shack is the main place to eat at the water park. Order at the window and carry your tray back to the sand.

reef-bar.pitch: Margaritas, cold beer and virgin coladas with your feet in the sand.
description: Reef Bar faces the wave bay. It serves nachos and chips with queso alongside the drinks, and soft drinks for the kids.

shell-shop.pitch: Sunscreen, flip-flops, goggles and whatever else got left at the hotel.
description: The Shell Shop is the water park's only store. It also sells Isla Velaluz shirts and hats.

caracol-snack-hut.pitch: Snacks and drinks within sight of the kids' pools.
description: The hut is placed so a parent can buy a churro without losing sight of the cove.

monsoon-grill.pitch: Tacos and burrito bowls at the foot of the ridge.
description: Monsoon Grill is the quieter of the water park's two lunch counters, with shaded tables and a view of the slides.

palmetto-food-court.pitch: A big, bright food court that feeds the whole hotel.
description: Burgers, tenders, salads and kids' meals, open from breakfast to late. Families staying at Palmetto Court eat here most mornings before the buses leave.

palmetto-pool-bar.pitch: Poolside drinks and bar snacks in the main courtyard.
description: The pool bar serves margaritas, draft beer and virgin coladas, with nachos and fish dip for the table.

court-sundries.pitch: The hotel shop for snacks, shirts and forgotten toothbrushes.
description: Court Sundries stocks Isla Velaluz apparel and sweets along with the basics.

hacienda-cantina.pitch: The hotel's restaurant, built around a courtyard fountain.
description: Hacienda Cantina serves carne asada, enchiladas and fish tacos at real tables. It is open to everyone, not only hotel guests, and takes reservations.

coral-cafe.pitch: Coffee, pastries and breakfast burritos off the lobby.
description: Coral Cafe opens early for people catching the first bus to the parks and stays open through the afternoon.

coral-cove-pool-bar.pitch: A swim-up bar in the hotel's lagoon pool.
description: Cold drinks, bar snacks and a row of stools in the water.

hacienda-mercado.pitch: A small market in the lobby for gifts and essentials.
description: The Mercado carries park apparel, sweets and the things you forgot to pack.

keepers-table.pitch: The hotel's dining room: Gulf seafood with the lighthouse in the window.
description: Keeper's Table serves blackened redfish, crab cakes and citrus roasted chicken in a room that faces the harbor. Dinner reservations are recommended, and the window tables go first.

faro-coffee-bar.pitch: Coffee, pastries and avocado toast beside the lobby.
description: The coffee bar is where the hotel wakes up. Order at the counter and take it out to the harbor wall.

lighthouse-lounge.pitch: A quiet bar with a view of the beam.
description: The lounge pours cocktails, wine and draft beer and serves a short menu of bar snacks. It is busiest in the hour after the park closes.

casa-boutique.pitch: The hotel's shop, for gifts a little nicer than a park shirt.
description: Casa Boutique carries Isla Velaluz apparel and sweets, chosen with the hotel's guests in mind.

aurelia.pitch: The finest table on the island.
description: Aurelia is the signature restaurant of The Velaluz Grand: butter poached lobster, day boat halibut and duck breast with guava, served in a dining room over the water. Reservations are essential.

the-grand-terrace.pitch: Cocktails on the terrace, facing the sunset.
description: The Grand Terrace is the hotel's bar, open to the Gulf on three sides. Go for the hour before dusk.

grand-pantry.pitch: Coffee, pastries and light breakfast for guests of the Grand.
description: The Pantry is small and calm, with good coffee and a breakfast burrito that people talk about.

velaluz-atelier.pitch: Jewelry and keepsakes, in a shop the size of a walk-in closet.
description: The Atelier sells charm bracelets, cufflinks and a bead kit for younger guests.

marea-alta.pitch: The Paseo's seafood house, on the waterfront end of the promenade.
description: Marea Alta serves blackened redfish, crab cakes and lobster bisque with the doors open to the Gulf. It is the most popular dinner reservation on the Paseo.

brasa-y-sal.pitch: Ribs, grilled salmon and big plates from a wood-fired kitchen.
description: Brasa y Sal is the steakhouse-style restaurant on the Paseo, good for groups and loud birthdays.

nonna-lucias.pitch: Red-sauce Italian: chicken parmesan, fettuccine and fried calamari.
description: Nonna Lucia's is the family favorite on the Paseo. Portions are large and the bruschetta comes out before you have finished ordering.

paseo-cantina.pitch: Carne asada, enchiladas and guacamole made at the table.
description: Paseo Cantina has the biggest patio on the promenade and a long list of margaritas.

lantern-house.pitch: Katsu curry, bulgogi bowls and miso salmon under paper lanterns.
description: Lantern House is the Paseo's Asian kitchen. The dumplings are made in view of the dining room.

gulf-coast-burger-works.pitch: Burgers, tenders and mac and cheese, fast.
description: The counter-service burger spot on the Paseo, open late.

pollo-dorado.pitch: Tacos, burrito bowls and Cuban sandwiches at a walk-up counter.
description: Pollo Dorado is the quick, inexpensive dinner on the Paseo. Plantain chips come on the side.

dulce-paseo.pitch: The Paseo's bakery and coffee shop.
description: Dulce Paseo sells pastries, empanadas and cafe con leche from morning until the shops close.

the-salt-line.pitch: A cocktail bar with a long counter and a short menu.
description: The Salt Line is the place for a drink before dinner. Fish dip and chips is the thing to order with it.

rum-dock.pitch: An open-air bar at the end of the dock.
description: Rum Dock pours margaritas, draft beer and frozen drinks, with live music on concert nights.

velaluz-marketplace.pitch: The biggest shop on the island, with something from every park.
description: Velaluz Marketplace is the place to buy what you talked yourself out of earlier in the trip. It carries apparel, toys, pins, sweets and home goods under one roof.

coastal-thread-co.pitch: Shirts, hoodies and hats, and only that.
description: Coastal Thread Co. stocks the full range of park apparel in every size.

brinewood-home.pitch: Beach towels, kitchen goods and ornaments for the house.
description: Brinewood Home sells the souvenirs that end up being used: mugs, towels, picture books and holiday ornaments.
Plush, building sets and bubble blasters, with Farol the lighthouse cat in the window.

sugar-reef-candy.pitch: Fudge, caramel corn and chocolate sea shells.
description: Sugar Reef makes its fudge in the shop and hands out samples at the door.

faro-jewelers.pitch: Charm bracelets, cufflinks and small things in small boxes.
description: Faro Jewelers is the Paseo's jewelry counter, with a bead kit for kids.

paseo-surf-and-sport.pitch: Board shorts, flip-flops and gear for the beach.
description: Paseo Surf & Sport outfits people on their way to the water park, and carries Isla Velaluz apparel as well.

the-pin-exchange.pitch: Every collectible pin on the island, in one small shop.
description: The Pin Exchange sells the pins for El Faro, El Remolino, Constellation Coaster and the rest. Collectors trade at the counter.

paseo-kettle-corn.pitch: Kettle corn popped on the promenade.
description: You will smell it before you see it. The stand also sells churros, corn dogs and cold drinks.

limonada-stand.pitch: Frozen lemonade and quick snacks on the Paseo.
description: A walk-up stand for a cold drink between shops.

faro-bakery-and-coffee.pitch: Pastries out of the oven from park opening, and the first coffee most guests have on the island.
description: The bakery sits just inside the gate on the plaza, which makes it the first stop of the morning for a lot of families. Order at the counter, then find a table under the lantern strings outside.
The guava pastelitos are baked through the morning. The lantern sugar cookie is the one the kids ask for.

lighthouse-mercantile.pitch: The big shop on the plaza, and the last stop on the way out of the park.
description: Lighthouse Mercantile takes up most of one side of Plaza del Faro. It carries the widest range on the island: park shirts and hats, plush, pins, and the small things people forget to pack.
It is busiest in the hour before closing. Shop in the morning and you can have your bags held at the front of the park until you leave.
